title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: (19) carries a question mark in the manuscript: the claimed equivalence of d_P with an affine stratification is asserted tentatively. It is plausible in char 0 for smooth S/T, but 'without flatness of Omega^1' is not obviously enough, since the connection-stratification equivalence normally needs smoothness of S/T.
Minor: (16) should read H^1_DR(S/T, ...), the relative de Rham cohomology, rather than H^1_DR(S, ...).
The identification of hypercohomology H^1 with torsors-with-affine-connection is correct. Since quasi-coherent torsors are Zariski-locally trivial, the data are essentially Cech-type.

ideas.what: Relative Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology with E_2 = H^p_DR(S/T, H^q_DR(X/S)) via Gauss-Manin
ideas.modern_name: Katz-Oda spectral sequence / Leray spectral sequence for de Rham cohomology

ideas.what: A class vanishing fibrewise defines an element of E_inf^{1,n-1}, hence an extension of O_S by H^{n-1}_DR(X/S) as modules with integrable connection
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham normal function / extension class in Ext^1_{D_S}(O_S, H^{n-1}); infinitesimal invariant of normal functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (normal functions, late 1960s), Carlson (extensions of MHS, ~1980), Green/Voisin (infinitesimal invariants, 1980s), Saito (Ext in MHM)

ideas.what: H^1 of a de Rham complex with coefficients = torsors under H with an affine integrable connection d_P
ideas.modern_name: Torsors with affine connections / extensions of flat connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Deligne, 'Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers', 1970, for extensions)

ideas.what: Char-0 equivalence of an affine connection on a torsor with an affine stratification P -> P^inf(H)^+ satisfying delta(x+s) = delta(x) + (d^inf - delta^inf)(s)
ideas.modern_name: Affine (torsor) version of the connection/stratification equivalence; torsors under crystals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1968) for the linear case; Berthelot for the crystalline formalism
ideas.where_published: Linear case: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

missed.claim: Grothendieck (c.1972) builds, purely algebraically and over a general base T, the de Rham extension (torsor with affine Gauss-Manin connection) attached to a cohomology class vanishing on fibres. This is an algebraic, characteristic-general version of Griffiths' normal function and its infinitesimal invariant, phrased via torsors and affine stratifications. It predates Carlson's extension theory and Green-Voisin infinitesimal invariants, but this is only a sketch.
missed.quote: Nous avons vu qu'un tel objet s'identifie à une classe d'isomorphie de torseurs sous R^{n-1}f_*(Omega_{X/S}) muni d'une ... P -> Omega^1_{S/T} (x) R^{n-1}f_*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck viewing fibrewise-null classes as extensions of Gauss-Manin crystals. The affine stratification version (19)-(20) suggests a crystalline/positive-characteristic version of normal functions, relevant to p-adic Abel-Jacobi maps and syntomic regulators. Historically interesting but not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The Leray/Katz-Oda part is standard. The torsor/affine-stratification description of the extension attached to a fibrewise-null class is a neat early algebraic formulation of normal-function-type extensions, but it is sketchy, tentative ('?') and close to folklore.
